summary: Sensho Murakami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani and Toyo Universities under teachers including Ryomon and Yukitada Takeda. He taught at Tokyo Imperial University (professor 1917–1923) and Otani University (lecturer 1926–1928).

Seok-hyeong Kim worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Taisho University, he served as a professor at Dongguk University and as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University.

Seong-Uk Kim works in Buddhist and religious studies. Supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr. for his doctorate, he was appointed Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Seraphim Rose was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at USC, the California Institute of Integral Studies under Alan Watts, and UC Berkeley. From circa 1970 to 1982, he held a post with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes.

Sergey Malov was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, as well as linguistics. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and St. Petersburg University under Nikolai Katanov, later holding posts at Kazan State University and the National Library of Russia.

Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University, head of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and director of the Asiatic Museum.

Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University (attested 2000).
Sesso Oda was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded traditional teacher Zuigan Goto. As a teacher himself, his students included Soko Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Lee studied under doctoral supervisor Lee Sang-hae and held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Koh has served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Seungsahn Haengwon was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Dongguk University and trained under Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded in 1957. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. After completing a Ph.D. at the University of Manchester, he served as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).

Shagun Sinha specializes in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. Sinha earned a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University, where doctoral supervision was provided by Girish Nath Jha alongside instruction from several other faculty members.

Shailendra Bhandare is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He held posts as a curator at the British Museum, a fellow at Fitzwilliam Museum and St Cross College, and Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022).

Shaman Hatley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Harunaga Isaacson. He taught at Concordia University (~2007–2015) and became chair of Asian studies at UMass Boston in 2015.
Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She studied as a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and has served there as a project researcher (attested 2026).

Shaoyong Ye is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan. He subsequently joined the faculty at Peking University, serving as an associate professor (attested 2010–2016, 2026).
Sharon J. Roe works in religious studies and philosophy. Roe completed a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the doctoral supervision of Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

Sharon Salzberg works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University at Buffalo and under traditional teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Dipa Ma, and Sayadaw U Pandita, co-founding the Insight Meditation Society and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.
